results.title: Positive modal formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Positive and negative modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: every atom is positive, $\bot$ is positive, $\varphi \to \psi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is negative and $\psi$ is positive, and $\Box\varphi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is positive.

results.title: Negative modal formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Negative and positive modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: no atom is negative, $\bot$ is negative, $\varphi \to \psi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is positive and $\psi$ is negative, and $\Box\varphi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is negative.

results.title: Iterated box
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the iterated box $\Box^k \varphi$ is defined by $\Box^0 \varphi = \varphi$ and $\Box^{k+1} \varphi = \Box\,\Box^k \varphi$.

results.title: Sahlqvist antecedents
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The Sahlqvist antecedents form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every boxed atom $\Box^k p$ (an atom $p$ under $k \ge 0$ boxes) and every negative formula, and is closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\Diamond$.

results.title: Atoms of a modal formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set of atoms (propositional variables) occurring in a modal formula.

results.title: Sahlqvist implications
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A modal formula is a Sahlqvist implication if it is an implication $\alpha \to \beta$ whose antecedent $\alpha$ is a Sahlqvist antecedent and whose consequent $\beta$ is a positive formula.

results.title: Sahlqvist formulas
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The Sahlqvist formulas form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every Sahlqvist implication, is closed under $\wedge$ and $\Box$, and contains $\varphi \vee \psi$ whenever $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are Sahlqvist formulas with no atom in common.

results.title: The B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every atom $p$, the instance $p \to \Box\Diamond p$ of the B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula: its antecedent $p$ is a boxed atom with zero boxes and its consequent $\Box\Diamond p$ is positive.

results.title: Polycyclic groups (Kourovka Problem 13.11)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is polycyclic if it has a finite series of subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ in which each $H_i$ is normal in $H_{i+1}$ and each quotient $H_{i+1} / H_i$ is cyclic.

results.title: Almost polycyclic groups (Kourovka Problem 13.11)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is almost polycyclic, or virtually polycyclic, if some subgroup of finite index in $G$ is polycyclic.

results.title: Groups with a unique product presentation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has a unique product presentation if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and elements $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1} \in G$ such that every element of $G$ equals $a_0^{k_0} a_1^{k_1} \cdots a_{n-1}^{k_{n-1}}$ for exactly one tuple $(k_0, \dots, k_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 13.11 (torsion-free groups with a unique product presentation)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, asked by V. V. Bludov, that every group $G$ which is torsion-free (no element of $G$ other than $1$ has finite order) and has a unique product presentation is almost polycyclic.

results.title: A torsion-free group with a unique product presentation need not be almost polycyclic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Not every torsion-free group with a unique product presentation is almost polycyclic: there is a group $G$ in which no element other than $1$ has finite order, which has a unique product presentation, and which is not almost polycyclic.

results.title: Locally finite group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is locally finite when every subgroup of $G$ generated by finitely many elements is finite.

results.title: Composition series in Kurosh's sense
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S$ of subgroups of a group $G$ is a composition series of $G$ when it contains the trivial subgroup and $G$, it is totally ordered by inclusion, it contains the join and the intersection of every subset of $S$, and for every jump $A < B$ of $S$ (members $A \subsetneq B$ of $S$ with no member of $S$ strictly between them) $A$ is normal in $B$ and the quotient $B / A$ is a simple group.

results.title: Absolute simplicity of locally finite simple groups (Kourovka 11.108)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, asked by R. Phillips, that every locally finite simple group $G$ is absolutely simple: every composition series of $G$ in Kurosh's sense consists of the trivial subgroup and $G$ alone.

results.title: Locally finite simple groups need not be absolutely simple
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a locally finite simple group $G$ with a composition series, in Kurosh's sense, other than the series consisting of the trivial subgroup and $G$ alone. That is, the statement of Kourovka Problem 11.108, that every locally finite simple group is absolutely simple, is false.

results.title: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The set $M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of places of $\mathbb{Q}$, which indexes the inequivalent normalised absolute values on $\mathbb{Q}$. It consists of one infinite place, corresponding to the ordinary archimedean absolute value, and one finite place for each prime number $p$, corresponding to the $p$-adic absolute value.

reading_title.source: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$

results.title: Absolute value at a rational place
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value $|\cdot|_v : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ to the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ when $v$ is the infinite place. When $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, it sends $q$ to the normalised $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$, where $|0|_p = 0$ and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, with $v_p(q)$ the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.

results.title: Bundled complete normed field
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A complete normed field bundled with its structure: a type $K$ together with a normed field structure on $K$ for which $K$ is complete with respect to the metric induced by the norm. It is used to package the completed fields $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ at its places $v$.

results.title: Bundled completed field at a rational place
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: To each place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ this assigns a complete normed field: the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ with the usual absolute value when $v$ is the infinite place, and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers with the $p$-adic norm.

results.title: Completed field at a rational place
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is the field $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers when $v$ is the infinite place and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers.

results.title: Embedding of the rationals into a completion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the canonical ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ sends each rational number to itself, viewed as a real number when $v$ is the infinite place and as a $p$-adic number when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$.

results.title: Absolute value at the infinite rational place
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the infinite place of $\mathbb{Q}$, evaluated at $q$, equals the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ of $q$ viewed as a real number.

results.title: Absolute value at a finite rational place
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the finite place of $\mathbb{Q}$ at $p$, evaluated at $q$, equals the $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$ of $q$. Here $|0|_p = 0$, and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, where $v_p(q)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.

results.title: Norm of a rational in a completion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the norm in the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of the image of $q$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|q|_v$, the absolute value attached to $v$ evaluated at $q$.

results.title: The rationals are dense in each completion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.

results.title: Every nontrivial absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ is equivalent to that of a place
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).

results.title: The embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ into its completion at a place is an isometry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $v$ be a place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, and let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$. The canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the metric $d(x, y) = |x - y|_v$, into $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is an isometry: for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$, the distance between the images of $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|x - y|_v$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Quadratic form of an integer matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries, the quadratic form of $Q$ is the map $\mathbb{Z}^n \to \mathbb{Z}$ sending $x$ to $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$, where $i$ and $j$ range over $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. No symmetry of $Q$ is assumed.

results.title: Integers represented by an integer-matrix quadratic form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries represents an integer $m$ if $Q(x) = m$ for some $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, where $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$.

results.title: Universal integer-matrix quadratic forms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries is universal if its quadratic form $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$ represents every positive integer, that is, for every positive integer $m$ there is $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $Q(x) = m$.

results.title: Conway–Schneeberger fifteen theorem

results.title: Quadratic form of a matrix

results.title: Natural numbers represented by a quadratic form
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Universal quadratic forms over a ring
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Integer-valued quadratic forms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ is integral if its quadratic form takes integer values at integer vectors: for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the value $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j$ computed in $R$ lies in the image of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $R$.

results.title: Generalized hyperharmonic Euler sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $k \ge 0$, complex numbers $r$ and $a$ and an integer $p$, the generalized hyperharmonic Euler sum is $S(k, r; p; a) = \sum_{n \ge k} H_n^{[r]}(k) / (n + a)^p$, where $H_n^{[r]}(k)$ is the generalized hyperharmonic number. A term whose denominator $(n + a)^p$ vanishes counts as $0$, and $S(k, r; p; a) = 0$ when the series is not summable.

results.title: Median Euler numbers
